South America, Africa and India are highlighted orange with white arrows from their southern tips all pointing to a glowing question mark on Antarctica under POINTING AT WHAT?, so I expect a video explaining why the continents' tips all point south and what they are pointing at, probably that they were once joined together around Antarctica.

A grey globe with pale white continents has a glowing blue crack running through the middle of a landmass, with no text, so I expect a video about a continent splitting apart or a new ocean forming, though at small size I can only tell it is a globe with a blue line on it.

A and B are statistically tied: round 2 has B 4/10 and A 3/10, and across both rounds A has 12/20 and B 11/20. Slot effects decided each arm's picks. The tie-breakers favour A, three to one: A has 4 of 20 first clicks across both rounds against B's 0 of 20, A's glance read states the title's promise directly, and the film's frame 1 is already built for A. The one point for B is that it drew no legibility objections. The open risk is A's Up next card: in 8 of 10 Up next exposures, all five personas called NO OCEAN grey, muted or small. An optional fix is to add chroma to the island cap, not more luma, then re-run gate.py and the 168x94 glance.

result.title_holds: Yes. Keep "Why Can't You See Most of Hawaii? (Look Down)" word for word. With the same image, A got 3/10 picks and 2 first clicks; D got 2/10 and 0 first clicks. That gap is within noise and confounded by slot (A had the top Home slot, D the bottom one). Round 2 models favour A (A > D in 92% of persona bootstrap resamples), while the pooled round 1 + round 2 model slightly favours D (+0.42 vs +0.02). There is no case to switch. D stays backup 1, but round 2 shows its title drew interest in all 10 exposures while the NO OCEAN image was blamed in all 8 skips. Two personas and the glance read said NO OCEAN does not say "sinking". If the stall rule fires, pair D with an image that shows subsidence, for example BIG ISLAND, its round 1 pairing at 7/10.
result.ep01_beats_control: No. The live control clearly beats the repackage. E (Not Just a Coincidence + POINTING AT WHAT?) got 8/10 with 5 first clicks; F and G got 0/10 each. All five personas picked E at least once and none picked F or G (sign test 5/5, one-sided p = 0.03). E won in every model and in 100% of persona bootstrap resamples. The host mix does not explain it: on Up next, E was picked 3/5 from the last slot next to both Astrum and Map Pack. The failure reasons were consistent. All five personas said F and G had no text and looked like stock renders or models. Four of five read "(Pangaea's Breakup)" as a lesson or as the video they were already watching. Three read "(Not Just a Coincidence)" as a promise of a real answer. F's glance read was Astrum's premise (a continent splitting). Do not apply the repackage. Retire final_ep01_1 and final_ep01_2, and soften the playbook section 1 diagnosis of the live thumbnail. Any future ep01 challenger must beat E head to head in a balanced round.

result.summary:
I scored all 70 trials (5 personas x 14 feeds) against r2_key.json and checked the result with a Plackett-Luce model under three slot assumptions and a persona bootstrap.

The decisions:
- ep02: keep the title, NO OCEAN as the default, ONE ISLAND as arm 2, and drop YOU ARE HERE for a 2-arm Test & Compare.
- Backup title: "Slowly Sinking" stays backup 1, but it needs an image that shows sinking.
- ep01: the repackage loses decisively to the live control, so withdraw it.

The sample is 5 simulated personas and 10 trials per arm. Only the ep01 result (8/10 vs 0/20) is solid; the ep02 arm differences are ties.

Round 2 had design flaws:
- Slots were seeded random draws, not the planned middle slots. The pooled slot term is about -0.24 per slot, so slot 8 carries roughly 0.19x the pick weight of slot 1.
- Host mixes differed between arms: Park Vibes was missing from B's Up next feed, and Map Pack was missing from E's Home feed.
- The fix for round 3 is the same hosts and the same or rotated slots for every arm.

Luma again did not predict picks: E, the darkest card at 62, won. NO OCEAN's complaints were about greyness, not darkness.
